What a signal looks like

When a monitor check fails, SignalForge emits a structured Signal — a typed observation with severity, value, threshold, and context. Here are some example signals from a production workspace:

payments-api-health → status_not_2xx
HTTP 503 received · threshold: 2xx · consecutive failures: 4 · env: production
14:32:18Z
catalog-api-latency → latency_p95_exceeded
p95 latency: 2,840ms · threshold: 2,000ms · severity: warning
14:31:05Z
payments-api-health → status_recovered
HTTP 200 received · downtime: 4m 32s · monitor resumed normal operation
14:36:50Z

Quick look: CLI

Install SignalForge globally and start monitoring in two commands.

zsh 
$ npm install -g @signalforge/cli

+ @signalforge/cli@0.9.2
added 47 packages in 3.2s

$ signalforge init

✓ Workspace created: acme-platform
✓ Config written:    signalforge.yml
✓ API key stored:    ~/.signalforge/credentials

Next: define a monitor and run `signalforge monitor sync`
